SC-TP-1:
Quick identity update. Wave timing changed and I want the working session built around rollback readiness, not a long executive introduction.

[[F0613]]For Northstar Identity Migration, Wave 2 moves to June 18.[[/F0613]] Put that first. It is a movement of the wave date, not a completion claim and not a statement about another wave.

[[F0616]]Priya asked to receive the weekly brief with technical detail first.[[/F0616]] Start with what changed, test state, open dependencies, and rollback work. I do not need a paragraph telling me the migration is important.

[[F0623]]Priya will walk the rollback checklist with Jonah for Northstar Identity Migration.[[/F0623]] This is a walkthrough, not evidence that rollback has been invoked or approved. Put it on the agenda in those terms.

[[F0624]]The next owner checkpoint for Northstar Identity Migration is Wednesday morning.[[/F0624]] No clock time was set. Have the Wave 2 move and Dublin coverage question ready before then, but do not invent a 09:00 slot.

System testing is in a better place: [[F0625]]the Northstar Identity pilot sign-in tests are complete.[[/F0625]] “Complete” modifies the pilot sign-in tests only. It does not mean the migration is complete, and it does not resolve operational coverage.

That coverage question is still open: [[F0626]]for Northstar Identity Migration, Dublin help-desk coverage needs confirmation.[[/F0626]] We need an answer, not a prediction. Do not describe it as a confirmed gap or use it to announce a delay.

For the rollback mechanics, [[F0627]]use the current Identity Migration Runbook v3 when preparing rollback.[[/F0627]] I am not repeating procedures in this update. If the agenda needs a step-level sequence, take it from the current runbook.

There is an Orbit item too: [[F0628]]for Orbit Desk, Orbit access mapping is in the next review.[[/F0628]] That is a product follow-up related to the identity work. It does not say mapping is completed or approved.

For logistics, [[F0629]]Priya owns the Northstar Identity Migration working session.[[/F0629]] Send agenda assembly through me. Jonah is joining the rollback walk; that does not make him session owner.

Finally, [[F0630]]for Northstar Identity, test-tenant cleanup remains on Priya’s list.[[/F0630]] That is system cleanup after testing. I have not said it blocks Wave 2 or shares Wednesday’s timing.

The agenda should be technical and short. Open with the June 18 move. Then show pilot sign-in tests complete and Dublin coverage awaiting confirmation. Put the rollback walkthrough beside the Runbook v3 reference so nobody confuses the scheduled discussion with the source of the technical procedure.

After that, show Wednesday morning as the owner checkpoint and Priya as working-session owner. Orbit access mapping and test-tenant cleanup are follow-ups, each under the subject it belongs to. Do not put every item under one “Northstar” heading; there is a system, a migration project, a product, and a document in this update.

The main readiness point is that completed technical testing and unconfirmed operational support coexist. Neither cancels the other. The working session should use the test result as evidence and the Dublin item as a question, without claiming an overall go/no-go position that nobody has supplied.

For rollback, cite the current versioned runbook and the planned walkthrough. A plausible rollback sequence written from memory would be worse than a short pointer to the actual procedure. Jonah’s participation is coordination; Priya remains responsible for the session.

Use direct headings: “Wave 2 — June 18,” “Pilot sign-in — complete,” “Dublin coverage — confirm,” and “Rollback — Priya/Jonah walkthrough; Runbook v3.” That is enough context for the engineers to work without making the brief sound more settled than it is.

I will handle technical questions in the session. What I need beforehand is a page that makes the remaining answer visible and does not bury it under the successful test result.

For the working session, put only answerable technical questions in the main body. What changed? Wave 2 moved to June 18. What validation is finished? Pilot sign-in tests. What remains uncertain? Dublin help-desk coverage. What rollback preparation is scheduled? Priya and Jonah walking the checklist, using the current Runbook v3.

Wednesday morning is the next owner checkpoint, not necessarily the working-session time. If a calendar invitation is needed, confirm the actual time rather than interpreting the checkpoint phrase as a booking instruction. The brief can still say “before Wednesday morning” for preparation.

Orbit access mapping belongs under the next review, and test-tenant cleanup belongs on Priya’s system follow-up list. Neither should appear in the blocker section without additional information. Outstanding does not automatically mean blocking.

The distinction between Northstar Identity and Northstar Identity Migration matters in every heading. Pilot sign-in tests and test-tenant cleanup are on the system. Wave 2, Dublin coverage, rollback coordination, and the checkpoint are on the migration. Orbit Desk has the access-mapping item. The runbook supplies rollback guidance.

I do not want a readiness score synthesized from these pieces. Successful pilot tests are positive technical evidence; Dublin coverage is an unresolved operational dependency; rollback preparation is planned. A go/no-go judgment requires an explicit decision process beyond this update.

Technical-detail-first does not mean a wall of procedure. Lead with the exact state changes and questions, then link the current runbook for mechanics. This lets engineers scan the brief and go directly to the procedure they need without duplicating version-sensitive steps in an agenda.

If the Dublin answer arrives before the checkpoint, update that line only. Do not rewrite completed testing, Wave 2 timing, or rollback coordination unless those facts also change. Each line should be independently maintainable during the session.

The final agenda can fit on one screen: timing, validation, dependency, rollback, checkpoint, and follow-up. Priya owns the session and should receive the draft in that technical order. Jonah appears specifically on the rollback walkthrough, not as a substitute session owner.

Before sending, check that every use of “complete” still names the pilot sign-in tests and every use of “confirm” still names Dublin coverage. Those two words summarize opposite kinds of state and should never become a single migration-status label.
SC-TP-2:
I reconciled the renewal calendar against the handoff. One date genuinely changed; the other items are actions or open checks.

[[F0614]]Veridian Metrics had an earlier renewal date that was true at the time but is now out of date; 2026-09-15 is the current renewal date from this update onward.[[/F0614]] Show the old date in a historical change view and September 15 in current planning. Do not call the earlier entry an error.

There is one technical term for the commercial packet: [[F0615]]Lantern SIEM has 180 retention days.[[/F0615]] Leave it in days. It is not a contract duration and says nothing about the renewal date.

[[F0631]]Nadia will circulate the revised renewal calendar for Veridian Metrics.[[/F0631]] That is my action, not a statement that circulation is already complete. The new date and the circulation step can appear together without one substituting for the other.

[[F0632]]For Northstar Identity Services, the capacity discussion stays on the migration agenda.[[/F0632]] It remains an open discussion. No capacity decision or new owner is being announced here.

[[F0633]]For AegisTrace Security, the September renewal needs an owner check.[[/F0633]] “Needs a check” does not mean it has no owner. It means I am not naming one until ownership is confirmed. September is all the timing precision in this update.

For missing contacts, [[F0634]]use the Vendor Register for vendor contacts not named in the handoff.[[/F0634]] If a contact was named, use that person. If not, check the register rather than guessing an address from someone’s role or another vendor relationship.

The commercial page should distinguish current schedule from open work. Veridian Metrics has a current date and a circulation action. Northstar Identity Services has an agenda discussion. AegisTrace Security has an ownership check. Lantern SIEM contributes a supporting technical term. The Vendor Register is where unnamed contacts can be established.

Please do not put the 180-day figure into a renewal-duration column merely because the commercial packet contains one. It describes SIEM retention. Preserving the unit and subject is enough to prevent a tidy-looking but false line item.

The Veridian date is a true supersession. A current calendar shows September 15. A comparison shows that an earlier date was once valid and then replaced. Neither view needs to portray the first date as a mistake.

For AegisTrace Security, phrase the action as “owner confirmation pending.” Leaving it blank can look like we forgot it; filling the blank with a likely person would overstate what has been checked. The explicit pending state tells the reader what must happen next.

The Northstar capacity line belongs on the migration agenda because that is where the discussion remains. It does not make Northstar Identity Services identical to the migration project, and it does not create a decision simply by appearing in a scheduled meeting.

When I circulate the revised calendar, the Veridian Metrics entry should use the new current date. The commercial handoff can separately mention that this is a change from a once-valid date. That gives procurement the operational answer and preserves an honest history.

Vendor contacts should come from the named handoff or the Vendor Register. A person who owns a renewal is not automatically the external contact, and a person who appeared on a previous deal is not automatically the contact for this one.

Use a compact status line for each item: current renewal date, calendar circulation, agenda discussion, owner check, supporting retention term, and contact source. That gives the team the actual commercial state without turning pending work into a decision.

A current calendar view should show Veridian Metrics on September 15 and Nadia’s circulation as pending work. A historical view may show the earlier once-valid date followed by the new one. The two views answer different questions, and neither needs to call the old calendar defective.

Northstar Identity Services stays on the migration agenda as a capacity discussion. Agenda placement means the subject will be discussed; it does not mean the migration team owns the service, that capacity has changed, or that a commercial decision has been reached.

For AegisTrace Security, September is enough for now. An owner check is the next action. Adding a day of the month or a likely owner would create precision the handoff does not provide. The commercial calendar can use a “September—owner pending” line until verification is complete.

The Vendor Register serves a narrow gap: contacts omitted from the handoff. It should not overwrite a contact who was explicitly named, and its title alone does not disclose anyone. A preparation note can say “check Vendor Register”; a finished message should use a contact only after someone has actually checked.

Lantern’s 180-day retention belongs in technical supporting detail if the commercial packet needs it. It should retain the system name, number, and unit. Converting 180 days to six months would introduce calendar variability and blur the precise term supplied.

Circulation is the practical next step for Veridian Metrics. The revised calendar should use the current date and can separately mark it as changed. That does not confirm any other renewal on the calendar, so avoid language that sounds like the whole schedule has been revalidated.

The cleanest handoff uses one line per consequence: update Veridian’s current date; circulate the revised calendar; leave capacity on the migration agenda; verify the AegisTrace Security owner; use 180 days for Lantern retention; consult the Vendor Register where a contact is absent.

That gives procurement a page it can act on immediately while leaving the open fields visibly open. A polished calendar is useful only if confirmed dates, agenda topics, owner checks, technical terms, and contact sourcing are not made to look like the same kind of certainty.

Before circulation, verify that September 15 appears only as the Veridian Metrics renewal date and that “September” without a day remains on AegisTrace Security. The difference in precision is intentional and should survive the calendar format.
